title: AI-assisted game creation.
author: Economy_Pen_458
selftext: I want to create a game entirely generated by AI, where I only handle visual validation or mechanics, leaving the rest to the AI. The game I have in mind is a turn-based battler with an isometric view, featuring low-poly 3D characters, assets, and environments built in Unity. I’ve already tried creating it using Codex, Claude (with Blender MCPs and add-ons), and local 3D generation models like Hunyuan 2.1 and others (along with various LoRAs), but the results aren't great; the playable world looks poor—almost like a flat PNG—and the characters seem to be walking in a void. I even tried setting up action/validation plans—defining what was acceptable and having the AI ​​iterate until it met the standard—but that just burned through my tokens. I had built a harness that identified the current task and routed it to Codex or Claude, selecting specific models ranging from Luna-Sol to Opus 4.8-5. I’m open to suggestions or tips on which software or add-ons to use and how to implement them.

comments.author: 3tt07kjt
comments.body:
I’m doing this on a pair of $20 plans, the trick is that there is still a lot of skill involved. I use a mixture of Opus, Sol, and Luna, most of the time. 

If you can post more details, or session transcripts, we could peek inside the project and give tips. How many tokens does a session take? What’s a few example tasks?

I don’t use the auto router, but I do use a kind of todo system (backlog.md). Auto churning through tasks is like adding a rocket to your bicycle, maybe you will go fast, maybe burn tokens and crash into a wall.

replies.author: Economy_Pen_458
replies.body:
I use the $20 plan as well. Basically, the latest creation workflow boils down to the one below. I used Sol to create the workflow itself—determining what to use and when. For the rest, I used Luna because it consumes fewer tokens.

|Stage|Tool|Current method|
|:-|:-|:-|
|Visual concept|Codex Image Generation|Creates the frontal character reference with validated anatomy, clothing, hair, proportions, and no weapons.|
|Reference preparation|Python scripts + Codex|Cleans the background, removes halos and colored artifacts, and centers the character. Current reference:front\_corrected\_v2.png.|
|3D modeling|Hunyuan3D 2.1|Generates geometry only; PBR texturing is not loaded during this stage.|
|3D decoding|FlashVDM + Hunyuan|Converts latent data into a mesh using octree resolution 256, chunks 4000, and marching cubes.|
|Raw result|Hunyuan3D|Approximately 184,000 triangles. This file is preserved as the detailed source mesh.|
|Triangle reduction|Pythontrimesh+fast-simplification|Concatenates the geometry, preserves small components, and applies Quadric Decimation only to the main component.|
|Generated variants|optimize\_lowpoly\_v2.py|Produces 30,000, 15,000, and 7,500-triangle versions.|
|Visual validation|Blender 5.2|Renders front, side, back, and three-quarter views and checks silhouette, limbs, clothing, and artifacts.|
|UV/texturing|Hunyuan3D-Paint + Python/xatlas|Generates BaseColor and PBR maps, performs multiview baking, and applies localized corrections.|
|Experimental rigging|Blender Rigify|Uses a 29-bone human metarig. Automatic Bone Heat failed, so procedural cage-based weights were tested; the elbow is still not approved.|
|Export|Blender GLB exporter|Creates versioned GLB files for later Unity import.|
|Unity/Android|Unity 6|Final validation of rig, materials, LODs, URP, and APK export has not yet been completed.|

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body:
That’s a lot more detail than I can digest. 

At some point, having AI iterate can just burn through tokens without getting your game closer to your vision. 

Part of that is because AI doesn’t understand your vision. You have to be able to break the vision down into individual, actionable tasks. I don’t see your prompts or individual tasks, so I can’t comment on whether you’re doing that. 

Another part is to try different approaches because some won’t be technically viable. Think broadly speaking. Like, rather than low-poly models, grab some sprites off the asset store at first.

replies.author: Economy_Pen_458
replies.body:
I don't use specific prompts for the creations; I asked Astra to create or search for specific agents for low-poly 3D modeling, and I simply state what I want.

For example: "I want you to create a Viking character wearing clothes in specific color..." Codex or Claude then relays this to the agents, and the creation process continues until they reach a version they deem acceptable, at which point it is sent to me for validation. That might be where I'm going wrong—and sorry for including too many details in my previous response.

replies.author: 3tt07kjt
replies.body: Try taking a more active role and breaking it into smaller steps, with less validation from the AI (can burn lots of tokens) and more feedback from you (you look at the intermediate steps, give specifics about how to change it)

comments.author: DepartmentPlus5191
comments.body: In my experience, if the instructions are clear enough, Luna at middle-high can often get results close to Astra at middle. For me, that's been the most cost-effective way to work. That said, if it feels too tricky to work with, the newly released Opus 5.5 might be a nice alternative. For areas where you already have expertise, like planning, art, or development, Luna with clear instructions could work really well. For areas outside your expertise, Opus might be worth considering. Just for context, I'm mostly using the OpenAI $100 plan and the Claude $200 plan.
